items.title: Rashied Ali and Henry Grimes interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 30, 2009
items.q: I pull on everything when I’m playing just with Henry because I’m dealing with just the bass.

ctx.x: Is there one of your hands or feet or one of your instruments that you find when you’re not really comfortable, and as you said you’re trying to find out where is it, whatever it is, do you find that you rely on something just to play more until you can really find it —

Well yeah, well you know I definitely have something that I can fall back on. You know I mean I have something that, I mean that’s my experience and my prowess and my experience, that I pull on everything when I’m playing just with Henry because I’m dealing with just the bass. You know I’m not dealing with horns and piano and all that. So I have to rely on my experience and prowess and so a lot of times I could get something, I could pull up on something that would get me through the mass, you know. It can get me…

lasts until it changes again. So, because it’s always different, it’s always changing. And then we keep up some stuff for maybe 20 minutes or 25 minutes, and then after a while we’ll sort of look at each other and go okay, this is, it’s time to leave this now. And bang, we quit. You know what I mean?
